title: Passing the same variable as multiple args creates dummy-argument aliasing — undefined per F77
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE SWAP(A, B)
C     If a caller writes CALL SWAP(X, X) -- passing the same
C     variable for both -- the F77 standard says the behaviour is
C     undefined. The dummy arguments A and B are now aliases, and
C     A = TEMP corrupts B before its value is read. The legacy code
C     'works' on aliased calls only by coincidence of compiler
C     ordering.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      REAL A, B, TEMP
      TEMP = A
      A = B
      B = TEMP
      RETURN
      END

      SUBROUTINE MAIN
      REAL X
      X = 1.0
      CALL SWAP(X, X)
      END
notes: Dummy-argument aliasing is one of the easiest bugs to port without noticing — Java/C# evaluation semantics quietly fix some cases (because the reference IS the same object), and silently break others. The spec must surface this whenever a subroutine writes to more than one of its args.
